key_insight: High-resolution power profiles of generative AI workloads can be systematically mapped and scaled to whole-facility energy models, enabling accurate infrastructure planning without access to proprietary aggregated data.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of publicly available, high-resolution power data and inconsistent reporting resolutions that hinder accurate whole-facility energy estimation and data center infrastructure planning for generative AI workloads.
method: Collect high-frequency power telemetry from AI compute (GPUs/accelerators) running representative generative workloads to build temporal power profiles.
Create a mapping pipeline that aggregates workload-level profiles into facility-level demand using scaling factors for racks, PUE, cooling and power-distribution losses.
Validate and calibrate the aggregated model against whole-building meters and propose generalized templates for planners to estimate infrastructure needs.
impact: Provides AI/ML engineers and data center planners with a practical, validated way to translate workload behavior into facility capacity and energy forecasts—reducing risk of undersizing/oversizing and improving cost and sustainability planning.
visual_elements: Time-series line chart: high-resolution workload power trace (short timescale) overlaid with aggregated facility load (longer timescale).
Sankey or flow diagram: mapping from per-GPU power → rack → room → whole-facility including losses (PDU, cooling, distribution).
Bar chart or scatter: modelled vs measured whole-building energy to show validation/calibration accuracy.
Icon set: GPUs/servers, meter, cooling/CRAC unit, and building silhouette to represent components and scale.
paper_title: Measurement of Generative AI Workload Power Profiles for Whole-Facility Data Center Infrastructure Planning
paper_authors: Roberto Vercellino, Jared Willard, Gustavo Campos, Weslley da Silva Pereira, Olivia Hull
